blocks.text: Masjid on the first night of Ramadhaan to find lanterns burning and the Book of Allaah being recited. To this he said (to Hadhrat Umar (RA)), "O Ibn Khattaab! May Allaah illuminate your grave as you have illuminated the Masaajid of Allaah with the Qur'aan." [^1]
Hadhrat Ubay (RA), Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA) and Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma (RA) Lead the People in Taraweeh

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) had all the people perform the (Taraweeh) salaah of Ramadhaan collectively, he gathered the men behind Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) and the women behind Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma (RA). [^2]

Hadhrat Umar bin Abdulaah Ansi reports that it was Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) and Hadhrat Tameem Daari (RA) who stood in the place of Rasulullaah ﷺ to lead the men in Taraweeh salaah inside the Masjid while Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma (RA) led the women in Taraweeh salaah in the courtyard of the Masjid. (This was during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar (RA)) However, when Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan (RA) became the Khalifah, he had both men and women follow one Qaari, who happened to be Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Abu Hathma (RA). Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) would instruct the women to stay back and they were only allowed to leave (the Masjid) after the men had all left. [^3]

Hadhrat Arjafa says, "Hadhrat Ali bin Abi Taalib (RA) used to instruct the people to perform the (Taraweeh) salaah of Ramadhaan and would appoint an Imaam for the men and another for the women. I was the Imaam of the women." [^4]
Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) Leads the Women of his Household in Taraweeh Salaah

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) reports, "Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) came to Rasulullaah ﷺ one night of Ramadhaan saying, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I have done something tonight (and wish to know if it was correct).' 'What is it, O Ubay?' Rasulullaah ﷺ enquired. Hadhrat Ubay (RA) explained, 'The women of my household said to me, 'Since we cannot recite the (entire) Qur'aan (from memory), we shall follow you in salaah.' I therefore led them in eight Rakaahs of salaah and then performed the Witr.' Rasulullaah ﷺ (approved and) did not condemn what Ubay (RA) did. The act is therefore established as a Sunnah because of Rasulullaah ﷺ's approval." [^5]
Ibn Shaaheen, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.284). Khateeb in his Amaalin and Ibn Asaakir have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.387).
